$comment: Single source of truth for the emulator both a laptop and CI boot. create.sh and create.ps1 read this file and produce the same AVD from it; a CI workflow reads systemImage/device/config to fill in reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner's inputs (see the ci block below) without checking in a second copy of these numbers. Changing any value here is a deliberate re-pin, not a tweak: it invalidates every capture taken against the old AVD as a comparison baseline. See README.md#emulator for why.

systemImage.$comment: packageId is what sdkmanager/avdmanager resolve. Everything else here is not consulted by either tool -- it is recorded so a human (or a CI assertion) can catch the day Google republishes the same packageId with different bits behind it. That has happened to public system images before; a package id survives it, a build id does not.

device.$comment: avdmanager's --device profile. pixel_6 rather than whatever the tool lists as 'latest' -- an implicit default drifts every time a new Pixel profile ships, which is the exact failure mode this ticket exists to close. The profile only supplies defaults; config below overrides the fields that actually affect reproducibility.

config.$comment: Written into the AVD's config.ini after creation, every run, so a laptop AVD created months ago converges to the same values as one created today. Keys map 1:1 onto config.ini keys; see create.sh/create.ps1 applyConfig.

ci.$comment: Handed to GRA-101 (owns .github/workflows/*, not touched here). reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner takes api-level/target/arch, not a packageId, so it cannot pin the build directly the way create.sh/create.ps1 do -- it resolves 'android-35 google_atd x86_64' through sdkmanager same as anyone typing that string would, and Google could republish under that tag. The mitigating step, left for GRA-101 to wire in: after boot, run `adb shell getprop ro.build.version.incremental` and fail the job if it does not equal systemImage.buildIncremental below. That turns an unpinnable input into a detected pin.
